newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds end up, tobacco debt widens.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds end up, tobacco debt widens.

text.p: Spreads on bonds of tobacco companies widened across the board after news of a potential ratings downgrade to firms with U.S. litigation exposure hit the Street, traders said.
"Tobacco bonds widened between five and fifteen basis points after the news," said one high-grade trader.
Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it may cut the ratings of tobacco companies with U.S. litigation exposure.
Philip Morris 6-3/8 debt due 2006 widened five to seven basis points to a 90 bid, 82 offer, while the 7-3/4's of 2027 widened 15 basis points to a 120 bid, traders said.
RJR Nabisco 8-3/4 percent paper due 2005 was quoted wider by about five basis points as well, they said.
Among the firms mentioned by S&P were RJR Nabisco, Philip Morris, Loews Corp, and B.A.T Industries PLC.
On Wednesday, news that tobacco executives and state attorneys general were in negotiations on a possible settlement of litigation against the industry, triggered spreads on tobacco debt to tighten.
Market players voiced surprise at the S&P announcement. They had previously speculated that a potential settlement would be viewed as a long-term positive for the tobacco industry.
"People were surprised that this rating came out now," said one high-grade trader. "There's still no agreement yet."
Pressure had been building on the industry to seek a resolution to mounting lawsuits and other legal problems.
Meanwhile, the corporate bond primary sector saw various issuers tap the market as the tone in the U.S. Treasury market improved, syndicate sources said.
Philip Morris senior unsecured debt is currently rated at single-A, while RJR Nabisco's senior unsecured debt is rated BBB-minus by S&P.
In the broader secondary market, high-grade bonds ended slightly higher, tracking an improved U.S. Treasury market; however, very light volume was seen by players.
Turning to the high-yield arena, the sector continued to see very little action as players attended a second industry conference hosted by Bear Stearns in New York City.
Earlier in the week, Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette's annual high-yield conference in Arizona, kept activity light as well.
Meanwhile, most of the focus in the junk arena on Thursday was concentrated on various high-yield offerings brought to market, dealers said.
Exide Holdings issued a 175 million marks in seven-year euro 144A senior notes to yield 375 basis points via lead manager Morgan Stanley. The deal was increased from an initial 150 million marks.
Federal Mogul Corp also sold $125 million in 10-year 144A senior notes to yield 200 basis points over Treasuries. The deal was upped from an initial $100 million size, market sources said.
Separately, Merrill Lynch & Co is expected to underwrite a $300 million two-part debt offering for Tenneco Inc next week, sources said.
The Baa1/BBB rated deal is expected to include $100 million in 10-year notes and $200 million in 30-year bonds. Both issues are expected to include a make-whole call provision, they said.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond closed up 12/32 at 94-17/32 to yield 7.07 percent compared with 7.09 percent at Wednesday's close.
